title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 2. The Purification of the Ashrama of Sannyasa
html:
The Lord asks the people of Kantakanagara for their blessing; in the dwelling of Keshava Bharati He "initiates" His guru into the mantra of sannyasa and accepts sannyasa; guru and disciple dance in kirtana

Verse 1

नृत्यावसाने भगवान्रुरोद
प्रेम्णा हरेः सोऽपि विभिन्नधैर्यः।
दृष्ट्वा तदा तत्र समागता वै
रुदन्ति ते प्रेमजलाविलाक्षाः॥१॥

nṛtyāvasāne bhagavānruroda
premṇā hareḥ so'pi vibhinnadhairyaḥ|
dṛṣṭvā tadā tatra samāgatā vai
rudanti te premajalāvilākṣāḥ||1||

nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ruroda — wept; premna — out of love; hareh — for Hari; sah — He; api — too; vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered; drishtva — seeing; tada — then; tatra — there; samagatah — those assembled; vai — indeed; rudanti — weep; te — they; prema-jala-avila-akshah — their eyes clouded with tears of love.

1When the dance was over, Bhagavan wept: love for Hari had shattered His composure. Seeing this, all who had gathered there wept too, their eyes clouded with tears of love.

Verse 2

ततः समुत्थाय हरिः सगद्गद-
स्वरेण तान्प्राह समागताञ्जनान्।
मां तात मातश्च विधेहि साम्प्रतं
शुभाशिषो येन हरिस्मृतिः स्यात्॥२॥

tataḥ samutthāya hariḥ sagadgada-
svareṇa tānprāha samāgatāñjanān|
māṁ tāta mātaśca vidhehi sāmprataṁ
śubhāśiṣo yena harismṛtiḥ syāt||2||

tatah — then; samutthaya — rising; harih — Hari; sa-gadgada-svarena — in a faltering voice; tan — to those; praha — said; samagatan — assembled; janan — people; mam — on Me; tata — fathers; matah — mothers; cha — and; vidhehi — bestow; sampratam — now; shubha-ashishah — auspicious blessings; yena — so that; hari-smritih — remembrance of Hari; syat — may be.

2Then Hari rose and in a faltering voice said to the assembled people, "Fathers and mothers, bless Me now, so that I may always remember Hari."

Verse 3

श्रुत्वाभिलज्जाकुलिता विवस्त्रा
गतास्ततस्ते प्ररुदन्त एव।
श्रीकृष्णप्रेमापरिपूर्णदेहा
बभूवुः सद्भक्तिरसेन पूर्णाः॥३॥

śrutvābhilajjākulitā vivastrā
gatāstataste prarudanta eva|
śrīkṛṣṇapremāparipūrṇadehā
babhūvuḥ sadbhaktirasena pūrṇāḥ||3||

shrutva — hearing; abhilajja-akulitah — overcome with shame; vivastrah — as if stripped bare; gatah — went; tatah — from there; te — they; prarudantah — weeping; eva — all the while; shri-krishna-prema-aparipurna-dehah — their bodies wholly filled with love for Sri Krishna; babhuvuh — became; sat-bhakti-rasena — with the rasa of true devotion; purnah — filled.

3Hearing this, they were overcome with shame, as if stripped bare1, and went away from there, weeping all the while; their bodies were filled with love for Sri Krishna, and they themselves with the rasa of true devotion.

Verse 4

तान्सान्त्वयित्वा निजदर्शनामृतैः
स गौरचन्द्रो भगवाञ्जगाम।
गुरोर्निवासं सह वैष्णवाग्र्यैः
श्रीकेशवाख्यस्य महानुभावः॥४॥

tānsāntvayitvā nijadarśanāmṛtaiḥ
sa gauracandro bhagavāñjagāma|
gurornivāsaṁ saha vaiṣṇavāgryaiḥ
śrīkeśavākhyasya mahānubhāvaḥ||4||

tan — them; santvayitva — consoling; nija-darshana-amritaih — with the nectar of the sight of Himself; sah — He; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; bhagavan — Bhagavan; jagama — went; guroh — of the guru; nivasam — to the dwelling; saha — together; vaishnava-agryaih — with the foremost Vaishnavas; shri-keshava-akhyasya — named Sri Keshava; maha-anubhavah — the great-souled.

4Having consoled them with the nectar of the sight of Himself, the great-souled Bhagavan Gaurachandra went with the foremost Vaishnavas to the dwelling of the guru named Sri Keshava.

Verse 5

नत्वा गुरोः पादयुगं निवासं
तस्मिन्स चक्रे करुणाम्बुधिर्हरिः।
श्रीरामनारायणनाममङ्गलं
गायन्गुणान्प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यः॥५॥

natvā guroḥ pādayugaṁ nivāsaṁ
tasminsa cakre karuṇāmbudhirhariḥ|
śrīrāmanārāyaṇanāmamaṅgalaṁ
gāyanguṇānpremavibhinnadhairyaḥ||5||

natva — bowing; guroh — of the guru; pada-yugam — to the pair of feet; nivasam chakre — took up His stay; tasmin — there; sah — He; karuna-ambudhih — the ocean of mercy; harih — Hari; shri-rama-narayana-nama-mangalam — the auspicious names of Sri Rama and Narayana; gayan — singing; gunan — the qualities; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered by love.

5Bowing to His guru's feet, Hari, the ocean of mercy, stayed there; He sang the auspicious names of Sri Rama and Narayana and Their qualities, and love shattered His composure.

Verse 6

तथापराह्णे नृहरेरवाप्त्यै
न्यासोक्तकर्माणि चकार शुद्धः।
आचार्यरत्नो भगवांश्चकार
कृष्णस्य पूजां विधिवद्विधिज्ञः॥६॥

tathāparāhṇe nṛhareravāptyai
nyāsoktakarmāṇi cakāra śuddhaḥ|
ācāryaratno bhagavāṁścakāra
kṛṣṇasya pūjāṁ vidhivadvidhijñaḥ||6||

tatha — then; aparahne — in the afternoon; nrihareh — of Nrihari; avaptyai — for the attainment; nyasa-ukta-karmani — the rites prescribed for sannyasa; chakara — performed; shuddhah — pure; acharyaratnah — the Acharyaratna; bhagavan — the venerable; chakara — performed; krishnasya — to Krishna; pujam — worship; vidhi-vat — according to rule; vidhi-jnah — versed in the rules.

6In the afternoon He, the pure one, performed the rites prescribed for sannyasa, so as to attain Nrihari2, while the venerable Acharyaratna, versed in the injunctions, duly performed the worship of Krishna.

Verse 7

ततः समीपं स गुरोर्हितार्थी
गत्वावदत्कर्णसमीप ईशः।
स्वप्ने मया मन्त्रवरो हि लब्धः
शृणुष्व तत्किं तव सम्मतं स्यात्॥७॥

tataḥ samīpaṁ sa gurorhitārthī
gatvāvadatkarṇasamīpa īśaḥ|
svapne mayā mantravaro hi labdhaḥ
śṛṇuṣva tatkiṁ tava sammataṁ syāt||7||

tatah — then; samipam — near; sah — He; guroh — to the guru; hita-arthi — seeking (his) good; gatva — going; avadat — said; karna-samipe — into his ear; ishah — the Lord; svapne — in a dream; maya — by Me; mantra-varah — an excellent mantra; hi — indeed; labdhah — was received; shrinushva — hear; tat — it; kim — whether; tava — by you; sammatam — approved; syat — it may be.

7Then the Lord, seeking His guru's good, went up to him and said into his ear, "In a dream I received an excellent mantra. Hear it — will you approve of it?"

Verse 8

वारत्रयं तच्छ्रवणान्तिकं स्वयं
प्रोवाच न्यासोक्तमनुं विशुद्धम्।
श्रुत्वावदत्सोऽपि हरेरिदं स्या-
त्सन्न्यासमन्त्रं परमं पवित्रम्॥८॥

vāratrayaṁ tacchravaṇāntikaṁ svayaṁ
provāca nyāsoktamanuṁ viśuddham|
śrutvāvadatso'pi hareridaṁ syā-
tsannyāsamantraṁ paramaṁ pavitram||8||

vara-trayam — three times; tat-shravana-antikam — close to his ear; svayam — Himself; provacha — spoke; nyasa-ukta-manum — the mantra prescribed for sannyasa; vishuddham — pure; shrutva — hearing; avadat — said; sah — he; api — too; hareh — to Hari; idam — this; syat — must be; sannyasa-mantram — the mantra of sannyasa; paramam — supreme; pavitram — purifying.

8And three times He Himself spoke into his very ear the pure mantra prescribed for sannyasa. Hearing it, the other replied to Hari, "This is indeed the mantra of sannyasa, supreme and purifying."

Verse 9

व्याजेन दीक्षां गुरवे स दत्त्वा
लोकैकनाथो गुरुरव्ययात्मा।
गुरो ददस्वाद्य मनीषितं मे
सन्न्यासमित्याह पुटाञ्जलिः प्रभुः॥९॥

vyājena dīkṣāṁ gurave sa dattvā
lokaikanātho gururavyayātmā|
guro dadasvādya manīṣitaṁ me
sannyāsamityāha puṭāñjaliḥ prabhuḥ||9||

vyajena — under a pretext; diksham — initiation; gurave — to the guru; sah — He; dattva — having given; loka-eka-nathah — the one Lord of the worlds; guruh — the guru; avyaya-atma — the changeless Self; guro — O guru; dadasva — give; adya — today; manishitam — longed-for; me — to Me; sannyasam — sannyasa; iti — thus; aha — said; puta-anjalih — with joined palms; prabhuh — the Lord.

9Thus the one Lord of the worlds, the changeless, eternal guru, under a pretext gave initiation to His own guru3. And with joined palms the Lord said, "O guru, grant Me today the sannyasa I long for."

Verse 10

ततः शुभे सङ्क्रमणे रवेः क्षणे
कुम्भं प्रयाति मकरान्मनीषी।
सन्न्यासमन्त्रं प्रददौ महात्मा
श्रीकेशवाख्यो हरये विधानवित्॥१०॥

tataḥ śubhe saṅkramaṇe raveḥ kṣaṇe
kumbhaṁ prayāti makarānmanīṣī|
sannyāsamantraṁ pradadau mahātmā
śrīkeśavākhyo haraye vidhānavit||10||

tatah — then; shubhe — at the auspicious; sankramane — transit; raveh — of the sun; kshane — at the moment; kumbham — into Aquarius; prayati — as it passes; makarat — from Capricorn; manishi — the wise; sannyasa-mantram — the mantra of sannyasa; pradadau — gave; maha-atma — the great soul; shri-keshava-akhyah — named Sri Keshava; haraye — to Hari; vidhana-vit — versed in the rite.

10And at the auspicious moment when the sun passes from Capricorn into Aquarius4, the wise Sri Keshava, a great soul versed in the rite, gave Hari the mantra of sannyasa.

Verse 11

ततः सरोमाञ्चितदेहयष्टि-
रानन्दनेत्राम्बुभिरार्द्रवक्षाः।
संन्यस्त एवाहमिति स्वयं हरिः
सगद्गदं वाक्यमुवाच देवः॥११॥

tataḥ saromāñcitadehayaṣṭi-
rānandanetrāmbubhirārdravakṣāḥ|
saṁnyasta evāhamiti svayaṁ hariḥ
sagadgadaṁ vākyamuvāca devaḥ||11||

tatah — then; sa-romanchita-deha-yashtih — His slender body thrilling with rapture; ananda-netra-ambubhih — with tears of bliss from His eyes; ardra-vakshah — His chest wet; samnyastah — renounced; eva — truly; aham — I; iti — thus; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari; sa-gadgadam — in a faltering voice; vakyam — the words; uvacha — spoke; devah — the Lord.

11And then Hari's slender body thrilled with rapture, His chest grew wet with tears of bliss, and the Lord Himself said in a faltering voice, "I have truly renounced the world!"

Verse 12

गच्छन्तमालोक्य हरिं गुरुः स्वयं
दण्डं सचेलं त्वरया ददौ करे।
भो भो गृहाणेति वदन्गुरोर्वचः
श्रुत्वा गृहीत्वा गुरुभक्तिलम्पटः॥१२॥

gacchantamālokya hariṁ guruḥ svayaṁ
daṇḍaṁ sacelaṁ tvarayā dadau kare|
bho bho gṛhāṇeti vadangurorvacaḥ
śrutvā gṛhītvā gurubhaktilampaṭaḥ||12||

gachchhantam — going away; alokya — seeing; harim — Hari; guruh — the guru; svayam — himself; dandam — the staff; sa-chelam — with the cloth; tvaraya — hastily; dadau — placed; kare — in His hand; bho bho — ho there; grihana — take; iti — thus; vadan — saying; guroh — of the guru; vachah — the word; shrutva — hearing; grihitva — taking (it); guru-bhakti-lampatah — eager in devotion to the guru.

12Seeing Hari about to leave, the guru himself hastily placed the staff, together with the cloth, in His hand, saying, "Ho there, ho there, take it!" Hearing the guru's word, Hari, eager in devotion to His guru, accepted them,

Verse 13

गुरोर्निदेशं बहुमन्यमान-
स्तत्रावसत्तद्दिवसं जितारिः।
रात्रौ वसन्कीर्तनमाशु चक्रे
नृत्यं च तस्मिन्गुरुणा समं प्रभुः॥१३॥

gurornideśaṁ bahumanyamāna-
statrāvasattaddivasaṁ jitāriḥ|
rātrau vasankīrtanamāśu cakre
nṛtyaṁ ca tasminguruṇā samaṁ prabhuḥ||13||

guroh — of the guru; nidesham — the command; bahu-manyamanah — honouring highly; tatra — there; avasat — stayed; tat-divasam — that day; jita-arih — the conqueror of foes; ratrau — at night; vasan — staying; kirtanam — kirtana; ashu — soon; chakre — began; nrityam — dancing; cha — and; tasmin — there; guruna samam — together with the guru; prabhuh — the Lord.

13and, honouring His guru's command, He, the conqueror of foes, stayed there that day. And at night the Lord soon began kirtana and dancing there together with the guru.

Verse 14

ननर्त तस्मिञ्जगतां गुरोर्गुरुः
कृष्णेन सार्धं महता सुखेन।
आनन्दपूर्णस्तु पुनः स मेने
ब्राह्मं सुखं तुच्छतरं महात्मा॥१४॥

nanarta tasmiñjagatāṁ gurorguruḥ
kṛṣṇena sārdhaṁ mahatā sukhena|
ānandapūrṇastu punaḥ sa mene
brāhmaṁ sukhaṁ tucchataraṁ mahātmā||14||

nanarta — danced; tasmin — there; jagatam — of the worlds; guroh — of the guru; guruh — the guru; krishnena sardham — together with Krishna; mahata — with great; sukhena — happiness; ananda-purnah — filled with bliss; tu — and; punah — then; sah — he; mene — considered; brahmam — of Brahman; sukham — the happiness; tuchchha-taram — most paltry; maha-atma — the great soul.

14There the guru of the Teacher of the worlds5 danced together with Krishna in great happiness; filled with bliss, the great soul now held the happiness of Brahman to be utterly paltry.

Verse 15

नृत्यावसाने हरिमब्रवीत्स
कोऽपीह मे दण्डमिमं कराग्रात्।
आकृष्य मां प्राह भुजद्वयेन
स्पृष्ट्वा स्वयं त्वं नटनं कुरुष्व॥१५॥

nṛtyāvasāne harimabravītsa
ko'pīha me daṇḍamimaṁ karāgrāt|
ākṛṣya māṁ prāha bhujadvayena
spṛṣṭvā svayaṁ tvaṁ naṭanaṁ kuruṣva||15||

nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; harim — to Hari; abravit — said; sah — he; ko api — someone; iha — here; me — my; dandam — staff; imam — this; kara-agrat — from my hand; akrishya — snatching; mam — to me; praha — said; bhuja-dvayena — with both arms; sprishtva — touching (me); svayam — yourself; tvam — you; natanam — dancing; kurushva — do.

15When the dance was over, he said to Hari, "Someone here snatched this staff from my hand, clasped me with both arms and said, 'You too — dance!'

Verse 16

ततोऽहमानन्दपरिप्लुतो मुदा
प्रविश्य नृत्यं कृतवान्सुविह्वलः।
श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य सुविस्मितास्ते
सवैष्णवाः प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्याः॥१६॥

tato'hamānandaparipluto mudā
praviśya nṛtyaṁ kṛtavānsuvihvalaḥ|
śrutvā vacastasya suvismitāste
savaiṣṇavāḥ premavibhinnadhairyāḥ||16||

tatah — then; aham — I; ananda-pariplutah — flooded with bliss; muda — joyfully; pravishya — entering; nrityam — the dance; kritavan — danced; su-vihvalah — beside myself; shrutva — hearing; vachah — the words; tasya — his; su-vismitah — amazed; te — they; sa-vaishnavah — together with the Vaishnavas; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — their composure shattered by love.

16And then, flooded with bliss, I joyfully joined the dance, quite beside myself." Hearing his words, all those present, together with the Vaishnavas, were amazed, and love shattered their composure.

Verse 17

श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यमनल्पमर्थव-
न्ननर्त तस्मिन्स्वजनैरनुव्रतः।
हर्षेण युक्तो महता महात्मा
स्वयं हरिः स्वात्मरतो गुणाश्रयः॥१७॥

śrutvā gurorvākyamanalpamarthava-
nnanarta tasminsvajanairanuvrataḥ|
harṣeṇa yukto mahatā mahātmā
svayaṁ hariḥ svātmarato guṇāśrayaḥ||17||

shrutva — hearing; guroh — of the guru; vakyam — the word; analpam — weighty; arthavat — full of meaning; nanarta — danced; tasmin — there; sva-janaih — by His own people; anuvratah — followed; harshena — with joy; yuktah — filled; mahata — great; maha-atma — the great soul; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari; sva-atma-ratah — delighting in Himself; guna-ashrayah — the abode of virtues.

17Hearing this weighty, meaningful word of His guru, Hari Himself — the great soul, delighting in Himself, the abode of all virtues — was filled with great joy and danced there together with His own.

Verse 18

स भारती प्रेमपरिप्लुतात्मा
कमण्डलुं दण्डमपीह दूरे।
क्षिप्त्वा ननर्त प्रभुणा समं वै
सन्न्यासधर्मस्य पवित्रहेतुना॥१८॥

sa bhāratī premapariplutātmā
kamaṇḍaluṁ daṇḍamapīha dūre|
kṣiptvā nanarta prabhuṇā samaṁ vai
sannyāsadharmasya pavitrahetunā||18||

sah — that; bharati — Bharati; prema-paripluta-atma — his soul flooded with love; kamandalum — the water-pot; dandam — the staff; api — also; iha — here; dure — far away; kshiptva — flinging; nanarta — danced; prabhuna samam — with the Lord; vai — indeed; sannyasa-dharmasya — of the dharma of sannyasa; pavitra-hetuna — for the sake of purifying.

18And Bharati, his soul flooded with love, flung his water-pot and staff far away and danced together with the Lord — to purify the dharma of sannyasa6.

Verse 19

इति स्वयं यद्भगवत्कृतं शुभं
सन्न्यासमानन्दकरं द्विजन्मनाम्।
शृणोति यस्तस्य भवेद्विमुक्ति-
र्लभेच्च तत्तन्मनसा यदिच्छति॥१९॥

iti svayaṁ yadbhagavatkṛtaṁ śubhaṁ
sannyāsamānandakaraṁ dvijanmanām|
śṛṇoti yastasya bhavedvimukti-
rlabhecca tattanmanasā yadicchati||19||

iti — thus; svayam — Himself; yat — which; bhagavat-kritam — taken by Bhagavan; shubham — auspicious; sannyasam — sannyasa; ananda-karam — bringing bliss; dvijanmanam — to the twice-born; shrinoti — hears; yah — who; tasya — his; bhavet — will be; vimuktih — liberation; labhet — will gain; cha — and; tat tat — whatever; manasa — in mind; yat — that; ichchhati — he desires.

19Whoever thus hears of the auspicious sannyasa that Bhagavan Himself accepted, which brings bliss to the twice-born, will attain liberation and whatever his heart desires.

Thus ends the second sarga, "The Purification of the Ashrama of Sannyasa" (Sannyasashrama-pavana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Literally "naked"; probably an image of shame: the Lord asks a blessing of them, His servants. The reading may be corrupt.
  2. Nrihari is here Krishna: Gaura, playing the part of a devotee, accepts sannyasa in order to attain Him.
  3. The Lord Himself speaks the mantra into Keshava Bharati's ear, as though initiating him, and only then receives it from him.
  4. That is, at the end of the solar month of Magha (January–February).
  5. Keshava Bharati, who became the guru of Krishna Chaitanya, the Guru of all the worlds.
  6. Hence the title of the sarga: sannyasa, accepted by the Lord and filled with love, purifies the very order of sannyasa.
